references.text: Aaron and his sons were entrusted to bless the people of Israel in the Lord's name, which is one of the central duties of priests mentioned in Deuteronomy 21:5.
Aaron and his sons were appointed to priestly service, emphasizing the selection of priests to serve the Lord.
The tribe of Levi was set apart to carry the ark of the covenant, stand before the Lord, serve Him, and bless in His name.
The priests and Levites were to decide difficult legal cases, consistent with the instruction that all disputes should be resolved by their word.
The Lord chose the tribe of Levi among all the tribes to stand and serve in the Lord's name forever.
The priests had responsibility to examine and judge cases concerning skin diseases (nega), as mentioned in Deuteronomy 21:5.
The Levites were appointed by King Jehoshaphat to judge matters of the Lord and disputes, in line with their role described in the books of Moses.
The priests are to teach the people the difference between holy and common, and in legal cases they are to judge according to the Lord's laws.
The lesser is blessed by the greater, which underscores the priests' authority to bless in the Lord's name.
